thread:
Maya: Heads up — started sanity run for Nimbus30B-v2 int4 bring-up with extended context (64k). Seeing divergence in outputs after ~12k tokens when we use our standard RoPE scaling patch.
Jordan: Divergence how? different tokens or "hole" in cache?
Maya: Token-level mismatch. Model starts generating but after long prefix it repeats a phrase it never picked in fp16 baseline. Logs show KV reads at later steps pointing to earlier positions.
Sahil: Could be phase wrap with our scaled RoPE once sequence index > 32768. Nimbus uses alternate rotary base (1e5) — maybe the scaling math doesn't commute with quantized kernels.
Leah: Screenshot of diff? paste some minimal repro pls.
Maya: Pasted run:```bash
./run_eval.sh --model=nimbus30b-v2 --quant=int4 --rope=scaled --ctx=65536 --test=longstory_10k
```
Maya: sample stderr: "KV_READ idx=65544 -> alias idx=872" then later "generated: 'and then the cat'" where fp16 had 'and then she said'
Jordan: That aliasing log looks like our circular buffer index math underflow. Are we using signed 32-bit indices in the int4 path?
Sahil: I checked the kernel patch — there was a cast to int that can wrap at 2^31, but we're nowhere near that. More likely the per-shard offset calc uses 16-bit in the quant path for perf.
Leah: Quick check — can you run with KV_DUMP=1 for one shard and attach the first/last 64 keys? I want to see if keys are shifted or repeated.
Maya: Will run now. Also note: when I rerun with rope=classic (no scale) int4, the mismatch disappears. So root cause tied to scaled RoPE + int4 path.
eval-bot: run queued: eval-1782 (Maya) — longstory_10k int4 scaled-rope; ETA ~4m; artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/maya/1782/
Jordan: Hypothesis: our interpolation used for scaled-rope relies on float accumulators. Quantized kernel performs an aggressive requantize step that truncates phase small deltas. When prefix grows, phase offsets accumulate error and indices map to wrong bucket.
Sahil: If that's true, workaround could be to force accumulation in fp32 for the phase step only. That will slow int4 path but useful test.
Maya: Running a variant now with PHASE_ACCUM_FP32=1 in env.
Leah: Also try a short sanity: seed=42, ctx=40k, compare token hash of positions 40k..40k+50 between fp16, int4-classic, int4-scaled. If hash differs it's not sampling randomness.
Maya: Dumped KV head/tail for shard0: head keys look fine, tail shows exact duplicate of keys at offset -32768. Attaching gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/mock-kv-dump-1766123456
Jordan: Duplicate with -32768 offset is a smoking gun. That's 2^15 wrap. Somewhere a 16-bit index being used.
Sahil: Confirmed kernel uses uint16 for ring buffer index in quantized jit for perf on A100. Need patch to promote to uint32 for >32k contexts.
Leah: Impact: dedicated workloads hitting >32k will corrupt cache under int4+scaled-rope. Do we have telemetry? How many customers on 64k?
Maya: Few internal tests only, but Redwood internal stress harness did a burst job last week. No customer hits yet but could for vector DB summarization.
Jordan: Prioritize: (1) hotfix kernel to use 32-bit indices in quant path (Sahil), (2) short-term guardrail: disallow int4+scaled-rope for ctx>32k in router (Leah), (3) add unit that fuzzes ring index rollover at 16/32/64k (Maya).
Sahil: Working on a unit patch now. I can compile and run quick smoke in ~15m.
Maya: eval-bot results: eval-1782 finished. Differences: fp16 vs int4-scaled divergence at token 12,142 for longstory_10k. Int4-classic matched fp16. Artifacts in s3.
Leah: Thanks. I'll open a rollout ticket to add the temporary router guard and add an alert if the kernel gets deployed without index fix.
Jordan: Also update Optimize recommendations: warn customers about enabling quantized scaled-rope at large ctx until this is patched.
Maya: Filing reproducible bug + small test cases now. Will paste PR links once Saahil's patch lands. :thumbsup:
Sahil: Quick update — patched uint16->uint32 in quant kernel, smoke run passes for ctx=65536 with scaled-rope. Pushing PR for review.
Maya: Nice. Once merged we should run full regression suite and a perf delta for int4 (expect small throughput regression).
Leah: I'll coordinate release gating and add a note in the release notes.
Jordan: Great catch Maya. Good teamwork.
Maya: Thanks — closing loop once regression and perf numbers are in.
